en.guide.archive.how1: Open Archive: on a phone, tap More, then Archive; on a computer, click your name at the bottom of the menu, then Archive.
en.guide.archive.how2: Find the item under Archived stays, Archived properties, Archived house-book entries or Archived operators.
en.guide.archive.how3: Tap or click Restore. For stays, properties and operators, Restore is in the row's menu (the three dots).
en.guide.archive.note: Archiving never deletes guest records. Only the six-year retention purge in Settings deletes them for good.
en.guide.archive.what: Archive holds the stays, properties, guest register entries and operators you archived. Archiving hides them from your daily work but keeps their history.
en.guide.archive.when: Use it to bring back something you archived by mistake, or to look at old records.
en.guide.archive.wrong1: An archived property is missing from the Dashboard and its guest link does not offer stays: restore it to use it again.
en.guide.ask.label: Your question
en.guide.business.how1: Open Properties: on a phone, tap Properties in the bar at the bottom; on a computer, click Properties in the menu on the left.
en.guide.business.how2: Tap or click the Business & legal details tab. Before your first property, tap or click Add operator on the Properties page instead.
en.guide.business.how3: Type the Company ID (IČO) and tap or click Fill from register. UbyHost copies the details from the public business register (ARES).
en.guide.business.how4: Check the Name, the Registered seat and the Tax ID (DIČ). Add the Contact email for data requests: guests see it as your contact.
en.guide.business.how5: Tap or click Add operator, or Save changes when you edit an existing one.
en.guide.business.what: The operator is the person or company that runs the accommodation. UbyHost uses its details for police reporting and on invoices, and shows its contact e-mail to guests.
en.guide.business.when: Add it before your first property, and change it when your company, address or contact changes.
en.guide.business.wrong1: Fill from register finds nothing: check the IČO, or fill in the fields yourself.
en.guide.business.wrong2: A property shows the wrong operator: open the property's Settings, Property information, and choose the right one under Property manager / operator.
en.guide.cleaning.add1: Open Cleaning: on a phone, tap Cleaning in the bar at the bottom; on a computer, click Cleaning in the menu on the left.
en.guide.cleaning.add2: Tap or click Add cleaning at the top of the page.
en.guide.cleaning.add3: Choose the property and the cleaning date.
en.guide.cleaning.add4: Write notes for the cleaner if you want to, then tap or click Save. Everyone with your shared link can read these notes.
en.guide.cleaning.add5: To change or remove a cleaning, find it under Cleaning dates and tap or click Edit cleaning. Remove cleaning is at the bottom of that page; the stay itself does not change.
en.guide.cleaning.auto: Every active stay gets a cleaning on its check-out day, marked After checkout. If the check-out date changes, the cleaning moves with it, unless you changed the cleaning's date yourself. If the stay is cancelled, its cleaning goes away. A cleaning you add yourself is marked Extra cleaning.
en.guide.cleaning.codes1: Tap or click Property instructions & codes at the top of the Cleaning page, then the property.
en.guide.cleaning.codes2: Write what the cleaner should do in Property instructions and tap or click Save. Every cleaning of this property shows it.
en.guide.cleaning.codes3: Under Door access code, type a code that already works on your door in Saved manual code and tap or click Save. If the property's TTLock lock is connected to UbyHost, you can tap or click Create permanent TTLock code instead.
en.guide.cleaning.codes_title: Instructions and door code for a property
en.guide.cleaning.share1: Tap or click Share schedule at the top of the Cleaning page.
en.guide.cleaning.share2: Tick the properties, then tap or click Create sharing link.
en.guide.cleaning.share3: Copy the link straight away and send it to your team: it is shown only once. The team sees the next 30 days, door codes included, and the link expires after 30 days.
en.guide.cleaning.share4: To stop a link early, tap or click Revoke link next to it on the same page.
en.guide.cleaning.share_title: Share the schedule with your cleaning team
en.guide.cleaning.what: Cleaning shows when each property needs cleaning, on a calendar and as a list, with the door code and your instructions for the cleaner.
en.guide.cleaning.when: Use it to plan the cleaning between guests, to add an extra cleaning, and to give your cleaning team a read-only link.
en.guide.cleaning.wrong1: A cleaning asks you to set valid checkout and check-in times: open the property's Settings, Property information, and set the arrival and departure times. The link Edit timing in Properties on the cleaning's page takes you there.
en.guide.cleaning.wrong2: A cleaning conflicts with the booking window: compare its date with the stay's dates and change it with Edit cleaning.
en.guide.cleaning.wrong3: A stay has no cleaning: cleanings are made only for active stays at properties that are switched on. Check the stay on Stays.
en.guide.cleaning.wrong4: TTLock could not confirm the code: try again, or save a manual code instead.
en.guide.cleaning.wrong5: The shared link reached the wrong person: revoke it. Revoking does not change a code they already saw, so change that code on your lock too.
en.guide.demo.body: Press Explore with demo data to try every screen with sample properties and stays. Demo records are never sent to the police. Use Clear demo data on the Dashboard when you are done.
en.guide.door_codes.how1: A code is created once every guest of the stay is registered.
en.guide.door_codes.how2: The guest sees it on the stay page and gets it by e-mail. You get a copy.
en.guide.door_codes.how3: The 24-hour rule: someone must type the code on the keypad once within 24 hours after its start time, or before it expires if the stay is shorter than 24 hours. Otherwise TTLock cancels it. A code starts 1 hour before check-in, so for a late arrival create a new code in the TTLock app.
en.guide.door_codes.how4: If the calendar moves the stay, the code moves with it and the guest gets a new e-mail. If the stay is cancelled, UbyHost deletes the code and tells you. A code nobody has typed yet may still work until its end, so check the lock in the TTLock app.
en.guide.door_codes.how5: Codes are created in TTLock's cloud, so they work even while the gateway is offline. Changing or deleting a code needs the gateway online.
en.guide.door_codes.how6: To switch it off, untick the property, or tap Remove on the Digital door lock page. Remove also takes away UbyHost admin access to your lock.
en.guide.door_codes.how7: Something changes at the last minute? You can always manage your own codes in the TTLock app. Open the lock, tap Passcodes, tap the code and change or delete it there. UbyHost only creates the codes it makes itself.
en.guide.door_codes.lede: Optional, per property. Connect a digital door lock and each guest gets a timed entry code once everyone on the stay is registered. For now this works only with TTLock locks that have a keypad and a gateway. Properties you do not switch on are not affected.
en.guide.door_codes.need1: A TTLock lock with a keypad, added in your TTLock app.
en.guide.door_codes.need2: A TTLock gateway near the lock, or a Wi-Fi lock.
en.guide.door_codes.need3: The lock's clock on Prague time: in the TTLock app open the lock, then Settings, Lock Time, and calibrate it.
en.guide.door_codes.shot_create-admin: Marked: Create Admin, at the bottom of the screen.
en.guide.door_codes.shot_home: Marked: 1 Authorized Admin, 2 eKeys (not this one).
en.guide.door_codes.step1: In UbyHost open Properties, pick the property, then the Door lock tab.
en.guide.door_codes.step2: Tick the box that accepts the door-code terms and tap Connect my lock. UbyHost shows a name such as hjhfa_uh1234abcd. Tap the copy button next to it.
en.guide.door_codes.step3: Open the TTLock app on your phone and tap the lock of this property. Use the TTLock account that owns the lock, the one you added it with. A lock that someone else shared with you cannot be connected.
en.guide.door_codes.step4: Tap Authorized Admin, then Create Admin at the bottom. Do not use eKeys: an ordinary eKey can only open the door and cannot create codes.
en.guide.door_codes.step5: Keep Permanent selected. In Recipient, the box that says Phone Number or Email, paste the UbyHost name from step 2. In Name type UbyHost.
en.guide.door_codes.step6: Switch on Manage their own users only, so UbyHost sees only the codes it creates itself and never your own codes or the codes of other people. Then tap Send.
en.guide.door_codes.step7: Back in UbyHost tap Check connection. Your lock appears with its name, ID and battery. If nothing appears, open Authorized Admin in the TTLock app and check that the UbyHost name is in the list.
en.guide.door_codes.step8: Open the property, section Door code. Tick Create a door code for each stay at this property, choose the lock, set the check-in and check-out time and save.
en.guide.door_codes.step8_title: Switch it on for the property
en.guide.door_codes.step9: Add a stay by hand for today, open its guest link and register. The code shows on the stay page and arrives by e-mail. Type it on the keypad within 24 hours after its start (see below).
en.guide.door_codes.terms1: Door codes are optional and run on your own TTLock locks. You stay responsible for access to your property and for keeping another way in, such as a key or your own code.
en.guide.door_codes.terms2: A code is sent only after every guest of the stay has registered. Anyone who knows the property's guest link and PIN can register for an upcoming stay, so keep the PIN private and change it from time to time.
en.guide.door_codes.terms3: The service depends on TTLock's cloud, your gateway and Wi-Fi, the lock's battery and clock, and e-mail delivery. UbyHost cannot guarantee that a code is created, delivered or accepted by the lock in time. Liability follows section 17 of the Terms.
en.guide.door_codes.terms4: TTLock is your own lock provider, a service of Hangzhou Sciener Intelligent Control Technology Co., Ltd. (China); it is not a UbyHost subprocessor. By setting up smart locks you instruct UbyHost to send it, on your behalf, the lock ID, each code's validity times and a reference number, never guest names or contact details. TTLock stores EU data in Germany, but has told us it does not consider itself to meet GDPR standards. Your relationship with TTLock, including any transfer outside the EEA, is yours.
en.guide.door_codes.terms5: UbyHost works on your locks as an authorized admin you appoint, through a TTLock account it makes for you, and never sees your TTLock password. It keeps that account's access encrypted and uses it only to create, change and delete codes and to read your shared locks and their clocks. It never opens a door remotely.
en.guide.door_codes.terms6: Door codes are stored encrypted and deleted one day after they expire.
en.guide.door_codes.terms7: Guests of every property that uses door codes see a paragraph about them in the property's privacy notice.
en.guide.door_codes.terms8: Door codes may pause when TTLock's monthly call limit is nearly reached.
en.guide.door_codes.terms9: You can switch door codes off at any time, per property or by removing the connection, which also takes away UbyHost admin access to your lock.
en.guide.faq.count_a: Calendars do not include it. It appears once the lead guest states the group size, or when you set it on the stay.
en.guide.faq.count_q: Why is there no guest count?
en.guide.faq.czech_a: Czech guests are not reported. Otherwise check the status: incomplete forms, Manual mode, or a paused login stop sending.
en.guide.faq.czech_q: Why was a stay not reported?
en.guide.faq.edit_a: Correct it on the stay and send again. A record the police rejected is not resent until you change its data, because resending the same data only adds another rejection.
en.guide.faq.edit_q: A guest made a mistake after the report was sent.
en.guide.faq.link_a: Check they have the current PIN under Guest links. Their stay is offered from the arrival day minus two days. If someone else claimed it, open the stay and press Unlink this e-mail under Guests.
en.guide.faq.link_q: A guest says the link does not work.
en.guide.faq.twice_a: Not by UbyHost. When the police answer is unclear, UbyHost sends that batch once more at the next automatic check, and an answer that the police already hold the guest counts as reported. You get an alert whenever an answer is unclear.
en.guide.faq.twice_q: Can a guest be reported twice?
en.guide.faster.search: Press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac) or / to search pages, properties, stays and reports.
en.guide.faster.shortcuts: Press ? for keyboard shortcuts: g d Dashboard, g s Stays, g r Police reports, g h Guest register, j and k to move between rows, Enter to open one.
en.guide.filters.body: Stay fees and Invoices share the same filter. Changes apply as soon as you pick them.
en.guide.filters.month: Month: use the arrows for the previous or next month. Stay fees always show one period (the last finished month by default). Invoices show all dates until you pick a month.
en.guide.filters.property: Property: shown when you have more than one.
en.guide.filters.reset: The number on Reset shows how many filters are active. Reset returns to the default view.
en.guide.filters.search: Search (Invoices only): part of the invoice number or the customer name, then Enter.
en.guide.filters.status: Status: on Stay fees needs setup, ready or saved; on Invoices awaiting payment, paid or corrections.
en.guide.finding.computer1: The menu on the left has Search, Dashboard, Stays, Properties, Stay fees, Cleaning, Payments and Settings. Help is at the bottom of the menu.
en.guide.finding.computer2: Click your name at the bottom of the menu to open the account menu. It has Settings, Contact support (the e-mail address of UbyHost support), Archive, Data requests, Keyboard shortcuts and Log out.
en.guide.finding.computer3: The button next to the UbyHost name at the top of the menu hides the menu. Click it again to show the menu.
en.guide.finding.how: Many pages have a ? button next to the title. Tap or click it for a short explanation and a link back here.
en.guide.finding.pages_title: Tabs and help on the pages
en.guide.finding.phone1: The bar at the bottom of the screen has Dashboard, Stays, Properties, Cleaning and More.
en.guide.finding.phone2: Tap More to open a list with Search, Stay fees, Settings, Help, Archive and Data requests. Log out is in the same list. Tap Close to go back.
en.guide.finding.phone3: The magnifying glass at the top of the screen opens search.
en.guide.finding.property: Open a property from Properties and it has three tabs: Overview, Bookings & calendars and Settings. Settings is split into parts, such as Property information, Guest experience, Reporting & fees and Automation.
en.guide.finding.search: Search finds pages, properties, stays and reports. Type a few letters, then tap or click a result.
en.guide.finding.tabs: Some pages have tabs under the page title. Stays has Stays, Police reports and Guest register. Stay fees has Invoices, Stay fees and Invoice settings, so you reach Invoices from there. Properties has Properties and, once you have added a business, Business & legal details. Settings has Settings, Archive and Data requests.
en.guide.finding.what: UbyHost has the same pages on a phone and on a computer. Only the menu is in a different place.
en.guide.finding.when: Read this first when you are new, or whenever you cannot find a page.
en.guide.finding.wrong1: You cannot see the menu on the left: the window may be narrow, so UbyHost shows the phone layout with the bar at the bottom. Make the window wider, or use the bar.
en.guide.finding.wrong2: A page is not in the menu: look under More on a phone, or in the account menu under your name on a computer.
en.guide.glossary.guest_link: One permanent web link per property. You send it to your guests, and they fill in their own check-in form on their phone.
en.guide.glossary.housebook: The list of every guest who stayed with you, Czech and foreign (in Czech: domovní kniha). The law asks you to keep it. UbyHost fills it from the guests' forms.
en.guide.glossary.ical: A calendar link from Airbnb, Booking.com or another portal. UbyHost reads your bookings from it. It gives dates only, no guest names and no guest count.
en.guide.glossary.idub: The number of your accommodation in UbyPort. It is in the letter from the foreign police. You enter it in the property's Settings, under Reporting & fees.
en.guide.glossary.lede: Short meanings of the words you meet in UbyHost.
en.guide.glossary.pin: Six digits that guests enter before the check-in form opens. Each property has its own PIN, under Guest links.
en.guide.glossary.stay: One booking at one property: the dates and the guests who come. Stays come from your calendars, or you add them by hand.
en.guide.glossary.stay_fee: The local fee (poplatek z pobytu) that a municipality charges per night. You collect it and pay it to the council. UbyHost counts the nights and prepares the report and a QR code for the payment.
en.guide.glossary.ubyport: The Czech foreign police system for reporting foreign guests. UbyHost sends your reports to UbyPort for you.
en.guide.guest_links.find1: Open Properties: on a phone, tap Properties in the bar at the bottom; on a computer, click Properties in the menu on the left.
en.guide.guest_links.find3: Tap or click the Settings tab, then Guest experience.
en.guide.guest_links.find4: Under Guest links, tap or click the copy button next to Guest link.
en.guide.guest_links.find5: Paste the link into your check-in message. Copy the Access PIN the same way and paste it too.
en.guide.guest_links.find6: To see what guests see, tap or click Preview as a guest.
en.guide.guest_links.pin1: To choose your own PIN, type six digits in Access PIN and tap or click Save changes.
en.guide.guest_links.pin2: For a random PIN, tap or click Generate a new PIN and confirm. Then send the new PIN to guests who have not registered yet.
en.guide.guest_links.pin3: Only if the link itself has leaked, tap or click Generate a new link and confirm. You get a new link and a new PIN, and the old ones stop working. Update your message on every portal.
en.guide.guest_links.pin_title: Change the PIN or the link
en.guide.guest_links.what: Each property has one permanent guest link and a six-digit PIN. Guests open the link on their phone, enter the PIN, pick their stay and fill in their forms.
en.guide.guest_links.when: You need them for every booking: put the link and the PIN in your check-in message on Airbnb, Booking.com and in your own e-mails. The same text works on every portal.
en.guide.guest_links.windows: Show stays starting within (days) sets how many days ahead a stay is offered on the link. Keep past stay links open for (days) sets how long a guest who forgot the form can still finish it through the stay's own link.
en.guide.guest_links.wrong1: A guest cannot find their stay: a stay is offered only when its arrival date falls within Show stays starting within (days). Check the dates on Stays, or raise the number.
en.guide.guest_links.wrong2: A guest's PIN is refused: they may have an old one. Send them the PIN shown in Access PIN.
en.guide.guest_links.wrong3: A guest says someone else already took the stay: open the stay and press Unlink this e-mail under Guests.
en.guide.guests.body: Guests open your property link on their phone and follow these steps:
en.guide.guests.cookies: The guest's phone remembers the PIN for 7 days, and the language, the claimed stay and submitted forms for 60 days.
en.guide.guests.czech: Czech guests fill in the same form. They go into the guest register and are not reported.
en.guide.guests.photo: Document photos are off by default. When a property requires them for foreign guests, the photo is deleted when you verify the guest, or 30 days after the stay. It is never sent to UbyPort.
en.guide.guests.step_claim: The lead guest states the group size and an e-mail address, then confirms from the e-mail. The stay then opens on that device only.
en.guide.guests.step_form: Each person, children included, fills in their own form: personal details, travel document, home address, a photo of the document when the property asks for it, and a signature.
en.guide.guests.step_mail: Guests get the private link, one reminder the day before arrival if forms are still incomplete, and a copy when all forms are done. You get an e-mail and an alert on arrival day if forms are still missing.
en.guide.guests.step_pick: Pick their stay by dates. Stays arriving today and in the next two days are offered.
en.guide.guests.step_pin: Enter the PIN you sent them.
en.guide.havel.body: Havel answers questions about UbyHost. Pick a topic or type your question. Check anything about filing deadlines against this guide.
en.guide.housebook.body: The guest register lists every guest, Czech and foreign, with their reporting state. Filter by property and dates, export CSV, or download signed PDFs as a ZIP (up to 100 at a time) for an inspection.
en.guide.invoices.body: Create an invoice for any stay or customer. The seller is one of your operators; VAT rates appear only for VAT payers. An invoice has up to four items so it fits one page.
en.guide.invoices.flow: Preview, then issue: the number is assigned per operator and year and cannot be changed. Afterwards you can record payment, e-mail it with a download link valid for 30 days, download the PDF, or cancel it with a cancellation or corrective document.
en.guide.invoices.how1: Open Invoices: on a phone, tap More, then Stay fees, then the Invoices tab; on a computer, click Stay fees in the menu on the left, then the Invoices tab.
en.guide.invoices.how3: Choose the Stay and tap or click Continue.
en.guide.invoices.how4: Fill in the Customer and the Items, then tap or click Preview.
en.guide.invoices.how5: If everything is right, tap or click Issue invoice. After that the invoice cannot be changed.
en.guide.invoices.how6: On the invoice you can Download PDF, Send to the customer's e-mail, and Record payment when the money arrives.
en.guide.invoices.settings: Before your first invoice, open the Invoice settings tab and fill in the Bank account for guest payments and the VAT status. The invoice number prefix and the default payment term are up to you. Then tap or click Save.
en.guide.invoices.when: Use it when a guest or a company asks for an invoice for their stay.
en.guide.invoices.wrong1: The stay is not in the list: add it under Stays first. The list holds stays from the last 400 days and the next year.
en.guide.invoices.wrong2: An issued invoice has a mistake: open it and tap or click Cancel / correct. UbyHost issues a new document that reverses it, and the original stays on file. This cannot be undone.
en.guide.invoices.wrong3: There are no VAT rates: they appear only when the operator is a VAT payer. Check the VAT status in Invoice settings.

en.guide.legal.disclaimer_body: UbyHost is software operated by the software operator identified in the Legal notice. It is provided as-is, does not provide legal advice, does not act as your data controller, and does not guarantee acceptance by the police or UbyPort. You remain responsible for correct data, timely reporting, signed forms, backups, and presenting records at inspection. When in doubt, contact the Foreign Police (reguby@pcr.cz) or a qualified adviser.
en.guide.legal.housebook_body: Under § 101 of Act No. 326/1999 Coll. you must keep a register of accommodated foreigners with the same data as the registration form, plus stay dates. Entries must be current, legible, and chronological. Keep them for six years after the last entry.
en.guide.legal.lede: UbyHost helps you comply, but the accommodation provider remains legally responsible. Read this section carefully.
en.guide.legal.paper_body: At inspection you must present the house book in written form. A screen alone is not enough. Download each guest's signed PDF (or the ZIP from House book) and store or print it. Signed registration forms count as house-book pages.
en.guide.legal.reporting_body: Report each foreign guest through UbyPort within three working days of check-in (§ 100). Czech nationals stay in the house book only and are not reported to the Foreign Police.
en.guide.legal.retention_body: Guest data is processed to meet your legal obligation (GDPR Art. 6(1)(c)). Keep records for six years. After that, delete them unless another law requires longer storage.
en.guide.legal.signature_body: Every guest record needs a signature before it is complete. Prefer the guest link so they sign themselves. If you type details by hand, sign on the host form. UbyPort will not send unsigned foreign guests.
en.guide.legal.verification_body: You are legally responsible for accurate police records. Check the travel document in person when your procedure or the law requires it. An optional upload does not replace that responsibility. If a guest refuses to show ID, you may refuse accommodation.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms1: Leon (AI) is optional and you switch it on per property. Leon is a chatbot that answers guests on the stay page and the QR guide page, only from the guide cards you write or import for that property. It runs on Claude, an AI model of Anthropic, PBC.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms10: Guests see in every chat that Leon is an AI, and the privacy notice of each property with Leon on gets a paragraph about it. Under the EU AI Act UbyHost provides Leon and you use it; do not hide from guests that they are talking to an AI. As the controller of your guests' data you answer their data requests, and UbyHost helps you, for example by deleting a chat early.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms11: Leon has message limits per stay and per QR chat, and it stops when the AI budget is spent or the provider is down; messages then go to you unread by Leon. UbyHost may change the limits and may pause Leon for a property or for everyone, for example for misuse, safety, cost or legal reasons, and tells you when it can. Any price for Leon is set in the price list, and we tell you before it changes.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms12: You can switch Leon off at any time for each property; chats already stored are deleted on the schedule above. If these terms change in a way that matters to you, we ask you to accept the new version, and Leon stays off for that property until you do.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms2: AI can be wrong. Leon may misunderstand a question or give an incomplete or wrong answer, even when your guide is correct. You stay responsible for your communication with guests and for the accuracy of your guide, so check your Leon chats from time to time.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms3: Do not rely on Leon for safety, medical, legal or access-critical matters. Keep check-in, key, door code and emergency information on the stay page or in your messages as well, and stay reachable. Leon points emergencies to 112 and tells you, but it never calls anyone.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms4: Leon does not make offers or decisions for you. It is told never to agree to prices, discounts, refunds, date changes, early check-in or other promises, and passes them to you. If a guest believes Leon promised something, you settle it with the guest. UbyHost is not a party to your contract with the guest, and liability follows section 17 of the Terms.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms5: You are responsible for your guide cards. Use only text you have the right to use, including text imported from your Booking.com or Airbnb listing. Do not put other people's personal data, such as a cleaner's private phone number, into cards without their permission.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms6: For each guest message that Leon answers, UbyHost sends Anthropic the guide cards for that page, the property name, the guest's message and up to six earlier messages of the same chat, including your replies. E-mail addresses, phone numbers and long numbers are removed from guest messages first; names and other words are not. Leon never gets guests' names or registration details from UbyHost.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms7: Anthropic is UbyHost's subprocessor for Leon. It is a US company and may process requests in any country where it operates, under the EU Standard Contractual Clauses. It deletes them within 30 days, keeps them longer only to enforce its usage rules or where the law requires, and does not use them to train its models.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms8: Guests can type anything, including health or other sensitive details. Leon gives no advice on these and passes them to you. Treat such messages with care, and never ask guests for sensitive data, payment or ID details through Leon.
en.guide.leon_terms.terms9: UbyHost stores the chats and deletes them 30 days after the stay ends, or 30 days after a QR guide chat was last used. You and the team members who can access the property see the chats. UbyHost staff open them only for support you ask for, for security or where the law requires. Our app logs never hold message text.

en.guide.overview.body: The Dashboard lists the stays that need you first, then stays waiting for guests, upcoming arrivals and finished stays. The four tiles count what needs action, what waits for guests, what is ready to send and what is overdue.
en.guide.overview.count: The person icon shows registered guests against the expected number, for example 2 / 3. Calendars never include a guest count, so nothing is shown until the guest states the group size or you set it on the stay.
en.guide.overview.deadline: Until a stay is reported, its row shows the time left until the police deadline. Red means less than a day or already late.
en.guide.overview.how1: Open Dashboard: on a phone, tap Dashboard in the bar at the bottom; on a computer, click Dashboard in the menu on the left. The UbyHost logo also takes you there.
en.guide.overview.how2: Start with What needs you. Each line says what is missing and has a button that takes you to the place to fix it.
en.guide.overview.how3: Below it, tap or click a stay to open it. View all stays opens the full list.
en.guide.overview.how4: Add stay and Add cleaning at the top of the page open the same forms as on Stays and Cleaning.
en.guide.overview.when: Open it first every time: it shows what needs you today, so you do not have to check every stay.
en.guide.overview.wrong1: No stays yet: connect a booking calendar so arrivals appear here on their own, or add a stay by hand (see Stays & calendars).
en.guide.overview.wrong2: A booking you expected is missing: Last updated shows when your calendars were last read. Check the calendar on the property's Bookings & calendars tab.
en.guide.overview.wrong3: A deadline is red: the stay must be reported in less than a day, or it is already late. Open the stay and check its colour (see What the colours mean).
en.guide.payments.body: Payments lists the payment requests you sent to guests and whether each is paid. To ask for a payment, open a stay and choose Request payment.
en.guide.privacy_requests.how1: Open Data requests: on a phone, tap More, then Data requests; on a computer, click your name at the bottom of the menu, then Data requests.
en.guide.privacy_requests.how2: Under Record a request, fill in when it was Received, the Channel, the Request and the Subject, then tap or click Record request.
en.guide.privacy_requests.how3: The request appears in the list with its due date.
en.guide.privacy_requests.how4: When you have dealt with it, tick Identity checked if you checked who asked, write what you did in Outcome note, set the Status and tap or click Save.
en.guide.privacy_requests.what: Data requests is your record of requests from guests or hosts to see, correct or erase their personal data. The deadline is one month.
en.guide.privacy_requests.when: Use it whenever someone asks what data you hold about them, or asks you to correct or delete it.
en.guide.privacy_requests.wrong1: You do not know what the guest's data is: open the guest's stay, or the Guest register, to see what UbyHost holds.
en.guide.reporting.body: Each property chooses when completed foreign guests are sent to UbyPort:
en.guide.reporting.deadline: The deadline is the end of the third working day, counting the arrival day when it is a working day. Weekends do not count.
en.guide.reporting.failure: If UbyPort is down, UbyHost retries on its own and alerts you. If UbyPort refuses the login, automatic sending for that property pauses until you save or test new credentials. If a send gets no clear answer, you get an alert and UbyHost sends that batch once more on its own at the next automatic check. A guest the police already hold counts as reported, so nothing is filed twice.
en.guide.reporting.filed: After a stay is reported, its deadline shows when it was filed, or how late if that was after the deadline.
en.guide.reporting.immediate_detail: Sent as soon as every declared guest form is complete.
en.guide.reporting.manual_detail: Nothing is sent until you press Send this stay or Send all ready stays.
en.guide.reporting.manual_filing_before: Outcome unknown: first check in the UbyPort web application that the guest is not already reported, because a second filing counts as a duplicate. You need the user name and password for the UbyPort web application from the "login details" document the foreign police sent you. They are different from the web-service access stored in UbyHost. Lost them? Call the UbyPort helpline +420 731 670 444 (working days 8:00 to 11:00) or write to ubyport@pcr.cz, with your IDUB or IČO and the property address ready.
en.guide.reporting.manual_filing_correction: Correcting an earlier report? Report the guest again with the right data and write in the note: PŘEDCHOZÍ OZNÁMENÍ OBSAHOVALO CHYBY ("the previous report contained errors").
en.guide.reporting.manual_filing_duty: The legal duty to report stays with you as the host, also when UbyHost cannot file. UbyHost does not check a report made by hand; the mark is your record of it.
en.guide.reporting.manual_filing_lede: Reporting foreign guests is your legal duty, within 3 working days from the start of the stay. When a stay is less than 24 hours from its deadline and still not reported, UbyHost e-mails you once for that stay. File the guests yourself if UbyHost shows a filing as rejected, failed or outcome unknown, if UbyHost warns that the deadline is close and the guest is still not reported, if UbyHost or the UbyPort web service is down while the deadline runs, or if your UbyPort web-service credentials are invalid or blocked.
en.guide.reporting.manual_filing_step1: Open the UbyPort web application at https://ubyport.pcr.cz/UbyPort/Home/Login and sign in with your own user name and password as the host.
en.guide.reporting.manual_filing_step2: Choose entering data in the web form (the manual entry module) and enter each guest who is not reported yet. You find their data in UbyHost under Stays > the stay > the guest, or in the guest's form PDF.
en.guide.reporting.manual_filing_step3: Send. On the result page click "Stažení dokumentu DORUČENKA – doporučeno" (download the receipt) and save the PDF. Check that the guest is in the list of accepted records, not rejected ones. Keep the receipt with your house book for 6 years, as proof that the report was made in time.
en.guide.reporting.manual_filing_step4: Then open the stay in UbyHost and press "I filed this stay by hand in UbyPort". Enter when you filed and, if you like, the receipt number. UbyHost then counts those guests as reported and never sends them. If you marked a stay by mistake, you can undo it within 24 hours.

en.guide.reporting.receipts: Police reports lists every report with its Doručenka receipt. You can download receipts one by one or as a ZIP for a date range.
en.guide.reporting.scheduled_detail: Sent a chosen number of hours (0 to 48) after the forms are complete, and never later than six hours before the deadline.

en.guide.settings.body: Settings hold your login e-mail, passkeys and authenticator app, the guest PIN setting, archived records, data protection (retention and deleting expired records), the activity log and technical details.
en.guide.settings.deletion: When your account is scheduled for deletion, a banner at the top of every page shows the date, 30 days ahead. You get an e-mail then and a reminder 7 days before. Until that date you can still sign in and work as usual. Download everything (ZIP) in the banner gives you the guest register as CSV, every guest's signed registration form, the police receipts, your invoices and your saved stay-fee filings (PDF and CSV). On the deletion date everything in the account is permanently deleted; records you must keep by law are then yours to keep.
en.guide.settings.email1: Under Account, type the New login e-mail and tap or click Send confirmation link.
en.guide.settings.email2: Open the link in the e-mail that arrives at the new address. Nothing changes until you open it.
en.guide.settings.login: You log in with a link that UbyHost sends to your login e-mail. That link always works, also when you add a passkey.
en.guide.settings.passkey1: Open Settings: on a phone, tap More, then Settings; on a computer, click Settings in the menu on the left.
en.guide.settings.passkey2: Under Security, tap or click Add a passkey.
en.guide.settings.passkey3: Confirm with Face ID, a fingerprint or your device PIN. Next time this device logs in without opening your inbox.
en.guide.settings.requests: Data requests records a guest's GDPR request and its one-month deadline.
en.guide.settings.retention: Guest records are kept 6 years after the stay, invoices 10 years. Document photos go after 30 days, raw police request data after 90 days.
en.guide.settings.two_factor: Two-factor sign-in uses an authenticator app. Store the recovery codes somewhere safe; each works once.
en.guide.settings.twofa1: Under Security, next to Two-factor authentication, tap or click Set up.
en.guide.settings.twofa2: Open an authenticator app, for example Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or 1Password, and scan the QR code. On the phone itself, tap Add to authenticator app on this phone instead.
en.guide.settings.twofa3: Type the six-digit code from the app and tap or click Enable two-factor authentication.
en.guide.settings.twofa4: Keep the recovery codes somewhere safe. Each one works once.
en.guide.settings.when: You need it to change your login e-mail, to log in faster with a passkey, or to add a second step with an authenticator app.
en.guide.settings.wrong1: You have a new phone for the authenticator app: use Move to a new phone under Security. You need a current code from the app or a recovery code.
en.guide.settings.wrong2: This browser cannot create passkeys: try your phone, or a current Safari, Chrome, Edge or Firefox. The e-mail link keeps working.
en.guide.settings.wrong3: You lost a device that has a passkey: tap or click Remove next to that passkey under Security. That device then has to log in with the e-mail link.
en.guide.setup.add1: Open Properties: on a phone, tap Properties in the bar at the bottom; on a computer, click Properties in the menu on the left.
en.guide.setup.add2: The first time, the page asks who runs the accommodation: tap or click Add operator and fill it in (see Business details below).
en.guide.setup.add3: Tap or click Add your first property. Later the button at the top of the page is called Add a property.
en.guide.setup.add4: Type the Name of the apartment: the name guests know from Airbnb, Booking.com or wherever they booked.
en.guide.setup.add5: Fill in the Address. Police reporting needs the municipality, the house number and the postcode.
en.guide.setup.add6: Under Managed by, choose the operator, then tap or click Create property. The guided setup starts.
en.guide.setup.step1: Under Properties, Business & legal details: the person or company registered with the police, with seat, IČO and contact.
en.guide.setup.step2: Name and address. The address and the UbyPort details must match the police letter exactly.
en.guide.setup.step3: Paste the iCal export link from Airbnb, Booking.com or another portal. Stays are imported and synced automatically.
en.guide.setup.step4: Under Property tools, Automation & UbyPort: the IDUB, mark, web-service login and password from the police letter, and when to send. Use Save and test connection to check the login.
en.guide.setup.step5: Under Property tools, Guest links: one permanent link and a 6-digit PIN per property. Copy the ready-made message into your check-in message on every portal.
en.guide.setup.what: A property is one flat or house you let. UbyHost needs its name, its address and who runs it. A guided setup then takes you through the rest.
en.guide.setup.when: Do it once for each property, before your first guests arrive.
en.guide.setup.wizard1: The setup has eight steps: Property details, Connect your calendar, Police reporting, Automation, Stay fee, Door lock, Guest link and PIN, and Test run. The top of the page shows which step you are on.
en.guide.setup.wizard2: Fill in a step and tap or click Save and continue.
en.guide.setup.wizard3: Connect your calendar, Stay fee, Door lock and Test run can wait: tap or click Skip this step.
en.guide.setup.wizard4: To stop for now, tap or click Exit setup. Later, open the property: its Overview tab has a Continue button.
en.guide.setup.wizard5: At the end, the Setup summary shows what is done and what is left.
en.guide.setup.wrong1: The form says Add an operator to continue: tap or click Add business details, save the business, come back and tap or click Check again.
en.guide.setup.wrong2: Police reporting asks for details you do not have at hand: they are in the letter from the foreign police. Tap or click Exit setup and continue when you have the letter.
en.guide.setup.wrong3: The address or the UbyPort details do not match the police letter: correct them in the property's Settings, under Property information and Reporting & fees. They must match exactly.
en.guide.statuses.failed: UbyPort rejected the record, the delivery failed or the outcome is unknown. Open the stay and act.
en.guide.statuses.incomplete: A guest started the form but something is missing, such as the signature or the document number.
en.guide.statuses.lede: The stronger the colour, the more it needs you. Every badge also has a word, so colour is never the only signal.
en.guide.statuses.not_required: Only Czech guests. They go into the guest register but are not reported to the police.
en.guide.statuses.other: The same scale is used everywhere: house book rows, reports, properties, stay fees and invoices. Amber always means you can fix something; grey is information only.
en.guide.statuses.ready: Everything is complete. In Manual mode you press Send this stay; in the automatic modes UbyHost sends it. Checking the ID is optional.
en.guide.statuses.reported: UbyPort accepted every foreign guest of the stay.
en.guide.statuses.waiting: Nobody has registered yet, or the remaining guests have not filled in their forms.
en.guide.stay_fee.body: A property takes part once you set its rate per night (up to 50 CZK). Set monthly or quarterly reporting, the variable symbol, the council account and the authority's details.
en.guide.stay_fee.pay1: Open Stay fees: on a phone, tap More, then Stay fees; on a computer, click Stay fees in the menu on the left.
en.guide.stay_fee.pay2: Pick the period with the month arrows in the filter. You start on the last finished month.
en.guide.stay_fee.pay3: Step 1 for each property: check the figures and tap or click Confirm figures. This freezes the numbers, so the PDF and the payment match what the council sees.
en.guide.stay_fee.pay4: Step 2: tap or click Download PDF and send it to the council, for example from your data box.
en.guide.stay_fee.pay5: Step 3: scan the QR code with your banking app and pay.
en.guide.stay_fee.pay6: To see the guests and nights behind the figures, tap or click Open report.
en.guide.stay_fee.rules: Guests under 18 on a night are exempt. You can exempt a guest for a legal reason, or charge one. Stays over 60 nights are not subject to the fee; an exactly 60-night stay needs your council's ruling first.
en.guide.stay_fee.save: When the period has ended and nothing is missing, press Save period. That fixes the report PDF, the guest register CSV and the payment QR. Start correction creates a new version; adjustments add or remove bed-nights without naming guests.
en.guide.stay_fee.setup1: Open Properties, tap or click the property, then the Settings tab and Reporting & fees.
en.guide.stay_fee.setup2: Under Stay fee (poplatek z pobytu), fill in the Rate per person per night (Kč), the Reporting period and the council's details, such as the Council account and the Variable symbol.
en.guide.stay_fee.setup_title: Set it up for a property
en.guide.stay_fee.when: You need it if your municipality charges a stay fee. Every month or quarter you send the council a report and pay the fee.
en.guide.stay_fee.wrong1: A property shows Set up stay fee: it has no rate yet. Tap or click Set up stay fee and fill it in.
en.guide.stay_fee.wrong2: There is no QR code: add the council's bank account in the stay fee settings and the QR code appears.
en.guide.stay_fee.wrong3: The figures were confirmed but are wrong: open the report and correct it there. Start correction creates a new version.
en.guide.stay_fee.wrong4: The account number is refused: check it against the town's website, or paste the IBAN.
en.guide.stays.add1: Open Stays: on a phone, tap Stays in the bar at the bottom; on a computer, click Stays in the menu on the left.
en.guide.stays.add2: Tap or click Add stay at the top of the page.
en.guide.stays.add3: Choose the Property, then the Arrival and Departure dates.
en.guide.stays.add4: If you know them, fill in the Number of guests, a Label for yourself and the Guest e-mail. All three are optional.
en.guide.stays.add5: Tap or click Create stay. The stay opens, and you can copy the guest link or add the guests yourself.
en.guide.stays.body: Stays come from your calendars, or you add them with Add stay. Update calendars fetches all feeds now. Filter by property, state and dates, save a view in this browser, and export the filtered stays as CSV.
en.guide.stays.calendar1: On Airbnb, Booking.com or your other portal, copy the calendar's iCal export link. Airbnb: Calendar, Availability, Connect calendars. Booking.com: Rates & Availability, Sync calendars.
en.guide.stays.calendar2: In UbyHost, open Properties and tap or click the property.
en.guide.stays.calendar3: Tap or click the Bookings & calendars tab.
en.guide.stays.calendar4: If a calendar is already connected, tap or click Add calendar first.
en.guide.stays.calendar5: Under Connect a calendar, choose the Platform and paste the whole link into iCal export URL.
en.guide.stays.calendar6: Tap or click Add calendar. UbyHost reads the calendar at once and tells you how many stays it imported.
en.guide.stays.calendar7: After that UbyHost checks your calendars on its own. To fetch new bookings now, tap or click Update calendars on the same tab.
en.guide.stays.cancelled: If a booking disappears from the calendar or is cancelled, the stay is cancelled and never reported. If guests had already filled in forms, you get a warning in UbyHost and by e-mail: when the booking only moved, set the stay back to Active.
en.guide.stays.dates_changed: If a booking's dates change in the calendar, the stay changes with it and guests do not sign again. UbyHost shortens each guest's dates to fit inside the new booking; a guest whose dates fall completely outside it gets the new booking dates. Each change is written to the activity log. A guest who was already reported keeps the dates that were filed, and you get a warning: check the booking, and if the filed dates are wrong, correct them in the UbyPort web application.
en.guide.stays.detail: Open a stay to add or remove guests, copy the guest link, send the report, change the expected number of guests, set the state (active, cancelled, ignored), reopen guest access or release the assignment, and create an invoice.
en.guide.stays.when: Use Stays to see every booking, to add one that is not on a calendar, and to check that guests have registered.
en.guide.stays.wrong1: A booking is missing: open the property's Bookings & calendars tab and look at Last sync. Error means UbyHost could not read the link. Check that it is the whole iCal export link from the portal.
en.guide.stays.wrong2: Last sync says Incomplete: the calendar suddenly sent far fewer future bookings than UbyHost has. UbyHost then cancels no stays until the calendar looks complete again.
en.guide.stays.wrong3: UbyHost says the calendar link is already added to another property: one booking calendar belongs to one property, otherwise every booking would be reported twice. Remove it from the other property first.
